evidence.domain: Compared against the WHATWG HTML tokenizer and real browser behaviour. Departures: comments are not tokenized (markup inside `<!-- -->` is treated as live), tag names are matched by `\b` so custom elements `style-x`/`title-x` are misread as raw-text elements, attribute names are matched by suffix so data-id and data-type masquerade as id and type, unquoted attribute values are ignored, SVG `<title>`/`<style>` context is not modelled, and `<script>` body ends are matched by `</script\s*>` (a browser also ends on `</script/` and `</script ` followed by attributes). A senior HTML-tooling engineer would require a real tokenizer (parse5) or a browser smoke test and would not accept regex tag matching. The hard parse-error gate for inline scripts (V8 SourceTextModule / node --check) is the right primitive and is correct.

defects.what: False positive: markup-like text inside an HTML comment is treated as live, so `<!-- <script> -->` or `<!-- <textarea> -->` reports '<script> is never closed' on a page Chrome renders fine. Violates the module's own no-crying-wolf rule; would turn the sweep red for a commented-out tag.
False positive: RAW regex `<(textarea|script|style|title)\b` matches custom elements such as `<style-guide>` and `<title-bar>` (\b between 'e' and '-'), reporting a nonexistent unclosed element.

False negative: scriptType regex `\btype\s*=` matches `data-type=`, so `<script data-type="x">` with a real syntax error is classed as non-JS and skipped; Chrome throws a SyntaxError and the checker passes the page.
False negative: declaredIds regex `\bid=` matches `data-id=` and ids inside HTML comments and script comments, so a lookup of an id that does not exist passes (Chrome throws a null dereference).
False positive: unquoted `id=price` (valid HTML5) is not recognised, so getElementById('price') is reported as a missing id.

Mutation survivors show test gaps: removing 'title' from RAW_TEXT_ELEMENTS and weakening the `opened !== closed` check both leave all tests green; the .mjs/.cjs choice is only tested when node runs without --experimental-vm-modules.

Sweep covers only ventures/; 11 research, 19 portfolio and 5 platform html pages are never checked, while platform/README.md says 'any product page'. Stale counts in comments (161 products, 61 tests) and no README in platform/webcheck/.

verdict:
Does not meet the bar (verification 2, correctness 2, claims 2; median 2); finished (completeness 3). The gate does its real job: it passes 3579 venture pages in 10.6 s, agrees with Google Chrome on 60 randomly drawn real pages (0 errors, 0 flags), and flags both historical dead-page failures plus missing ids, bad JSON-LD and conflict markers. But its regex pseudo-tokenizer disagrees with Chrome on 7 of 20 valid-HTML probes (comments, custom elements, data-* attributes, unquoted ids): two false positives that violate its own no-crying-wolf rule and two false negatives that let a syntax-error script or a null-deref lookup pass. None affects a shipped page today (greps find 0 matching pages). Of 5 seeded mutations the suite caught 3 (M3 only in CI's no-flag mode); removing 'title' detection and weakening the balance check passed all 63 tests.
